surprises.description: Operating diluted EPS of $1.27 was above the preview’s $1.19 headline consensus and within its $1.25–$1.30 bull case, but GAAP EPS of $1.16 missed that consensus. The GAAP result included a loss from pulling forward December investment-security maturities.
surprises.fact_evidence: Operating diluted EPS rose 16.5% year-over-year to $1.27. GAAP EPS was $1.16 and included a loss from pulling forward December investment security maturities.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed diluted EPS consensus of $1.19 and a bull-case EPS range of $1.25–$1.30.

surprises.description: NIM expanded 7 basis points to 3.56%, materially exceeding the preview’s expectation of a flat-to-slightly-down Q3 and its 3.49% FTE reference level. The preview expected a low-to-mid-3.5% year-end NIM, while management now expects a mid-to-high-3.5% exit rate.
surprises.fact_evidence: Net interest margin expanded 7 basis points to 3.56%; 3 basis points were attributed to selling $296.8 million of lower-yielding U.S. Treasuries and using the proceeds to pay down higher-cost overnight borrowings. Management guided to NIM exiting 2026 in the mid- to high-3.5% range.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management guided Q3 to +1 bp to −2 bps and expected a “low-to-mid 3.5%” exit rate for 2026.

surprises.description: The deposit rebound the preview was looking for was weaker than the headline growth suggests: deposits rose just 1.1% sequentially despite including $663.8 million of assumed Santander and ClearPoint deposits. That acquired amount exceeds the roughly $162 million net increase implied by the sequential growth rate, suggesting underlying deposits declined.
surprises.fact_evidence: Total deposits rose 1.1% sequentially and 5.7% year-over-year, including Santander assumed deposits of $543.7 million and ClearPoint assumed deposits of $120.1 million.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said deposits needed to rebound from the Q2 municipal outflow and called a failure to rebound the “cleanest bear tell”; it also cited management’s 3–4% full-year deposit growth guidance.

surprises.description: Full-year loan growth guidance was reduced to 5%–5.5%, below the previously stated 5%–6% target and the preview’s expectation that management would reaffirm it. Management cited seasonal consumer lending slowdowns and larger anticipated commercial loan payoffs.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management lowered full-year 2026 loan growth guidance to 5%–5.5%, citing seasonal consumer lending slowdowns and anticipated larger commercial loan payoffs.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited a 5–6% FY loan growth target and said the buy-side expected the loan-growth outlook to be reaffirmed.

surprises.description: Insurance shifted from the weakness the preview expected to persist to positive growth: revenue grew 8.9% year-over-year and pretax earnings rose 41%. The preview had described recent declines and framed stabilization as the item to watch.
surprises.fact_evidence: Insurance services revenue grew 8.9% year-over-year with flat expenses, driving 41% pretax earnings growth.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said insurance revenue had been down 4.8% year-over-year in Q2, management expected to miss prior guidance, and the watch was for sequential stabilization; its base case still had insurance negative.

surprises.description: Wealth Management growth accelerated well beyond its recent reported pace: revenue rose 41% year-over-year versus 19.8% in Q2, while ClearPoint added $2.1 million of quarterly noninterest revenue. The preview expected a first full quarter of ClearPoint contribution but did not anticipate this reported growth rate.
surprises.fact_evidence: Wealth Management revenue surged 41% year-over-year and pretax earnings rose 42%; ClearPoint added $2.1 million in quarterly noninterest revenue.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview reported Q2 wealth revenue growth of 19.8% and noted that Q3 would be ClearPoint’s first full quarter of contribution.

surprises.description: Employee Benefit Services pretax earnings fell 3.5% instead of continuing the growth the preview highlighted, as legal expenses related to new fund launches weighed on results.
surprises.fact_evidence: Employee Benefit Services pretax earnings fell 3.5% due to legal expenses from new fund launches.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited Q2 Employee Benefit Services revenue growth of 7.7% and pretax earnings growth of 16.2%, describing it as one of the fee businesses supporting the outlook.

surprises.description: Credit worsened from the preview’s expected non-event: net charge-offs rose 6 basis points sequentially because of losses on two business lending relationships. The allowance ratio, at 80 basis points, was also slightly below the preview’s cited 0.81%.
surprises.fact_evidence: Net charge-offs rose 6 basis points sequentially due to $2.7 million in charge-offs on two business lending relationships; the allowance was $92 million, or 80 basis points of total loans.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described credit as “currently a non-event,” citing NCOs of 0.12% annualized and an ACL of 0.81% of loans.
